Lim Wei Jie was a quiet, unassuming 32-year-old man guy who worked as a senior accountant in a mid-sized firm. Life in the humid bustle of the city moved fast, but his world had slowed to a single, burning focus for the past few years: Tan Mei Ling, his 27-year-old colleague in the marketing department.

Mei Ling was breathtaking—fair porcelain skin, long silky black hair that fell past her shoulders, almond-shaped eyes that sparkled when she laughed, and a curvaceous figure that her recent pregnancy only enhanced. At seven months along, her belly swelled beautifully beneath her sexy maternity dresses, her breasts fuller, her hips wider. She was married of course, but that meant nothing to Wei Jie. In his quiet fantasies, she was already his—warm, willing, forever.

Still, he stole glances across the open-plan office, memorized the sway of her walk, and imagined what it would be like to hold her, to taste her, to never let her go.

One humid Tuesday evening, Wei Jie went for his usual solo jog at East Reservoir Park, a sprawling green space where the city’s concrete gave way to trees and water. The sky was turning a bruised purple as the sun set. He rounded a quiet bend near the secluded eastern pond—rarely used after dusk—and froze.

There she was. Mei Ling, alone, in tight running shorts and a sports bra beneath a white tank top that hugged her pregnant curves She must have come straight from the office for some fresh air. She jogged lightly along the grassy edge, phone in hand, earbuds in.

Then her foot slipped on the wet bank. She tumbled forward with a sharp cry, plunging into the deep, dark water.

Wei Jie’s heart hammered. He ducked behind a thick clump of bushes, breath caught in his throat. Mei Ling surfaced, gasping, arms flailing. “Help! Somebody—please!” Her voice was panicked, water choking her words. She was a strong swimmer, but the weight of her belly dragged her down, and the pond’s edge was slippery clay.

He could have saved her. Ten seconds, a strong arm, a rope from his backpack. But he didn’t move.

This was fate. This was his chance. No more stolen glances. No more husband waiting at home. Just him and her—eternally.

He watched, hidden, as her struggles grew weaker. Her cries turned to gurgles. Her beautiful face, contorted in terror, slipped beneath the surface one final time. Bubbles rose. Then nothing. Wei Jie waited thirty long minutes, chest tight with a strange, tender exhilaration, until the water was glass-still. Only then did he emerge, strip to his boxers, and slip into the cool pond.

He found her easily—her body had floated a short distance, face-down, long hair fanning like black seaweed. Her skin was already cooling, lips slightly blue, eyes half-open in a vacant stare. He cradled her swollen belly against his chest, kissed her wet forehead, and whispered, “I’ve got you now, Mei Ling. You’re mine. Forever.”
Under cover of full night, he dragged her to shore, then carried her limp, dripping form through the trees to a disused gardener’s shed he had discovered months earlier—rusty lock long broken, hidden behind overgrown bougainvillea, far from any path. Inside, it smelled of earth and forgotten tools. He laid her gently on a weathered wooden table he had cleared, lit a small battery lantern, and locked the door behind them.

For the next five days, Wei Jie lived a secret double life. By day he was the same diligent colleague at the office, politely asking if anyone had heard from Mei Ling (the police had already begun a missing-person search after her husband reported her overdue from her jog). By night and early morning, he returned to the shed with supplies—bottled water, wet wipes and a cosmetics set.

He treated her like his beloved bride on a honeymoon. He stripped her wet running gear, washed her body tenderly with scented wipes, and left her in her sports bra and shorts that exposed her pregnant curves. Her skin grew pale and waxy, a faint greenish tint creeping in, but he didn’t care. Each evening he sat beside her, brushed her hair until it shone, and applied makeup with loving care: foundation to smooth her complexion, rosy blush on her cheeks, crimson lipstick on her cold lips, delicate eyeliner to make her eyes look alive and adoring again. “You’re still the most beautiful womantto me,” he murmured, kissing her painted mouth. “My perfect girl.”

Their “romance” was everything he had dreamed. He climbed onto the table with her, caressed her cool, heavy breasts, kissed down the swell of her pregnant belly, and made slow, passionate love to her lifeless body night after night. He whispered endearments—“I love you more than he ever could,” “You feel so good for me, Mei Ling”—while her unresisting form rocked gently beneath him. He held her close afterward, stroking her hair, telling her about his day at the office, pretending she answered with that soft laugh he remembered. The shed became their private love nest. The outside world—her frantic husband, the police divers searching the reservoir—faded to nothing.

By the fourth night her body had begun to swell further from the tropical heat, but Wei Jie still found her irresistibly beautiful. He touched up the makeup daily, sprayed her with his own cologne, and continued their intimate rituals with reverent devotion.

On the fifth evening, as the sun set outside and golden light filtered through the shed’s cracked boards, Wei Jie lay beside her again, one hand resting on her belly, the other between her thighs. He was deep inside her when it happened. The gases that had built up inside her decomposing form shifted with a low, wet sound. Her pregnant belly contracted violently. Wei Jie gasped in awe as her body performed its final act of “life”—a coffin birth. The stillborn fetus, perfectly formed but lifeless, slipped from between her legs onto the table in a rush of dark fluids.

Tears of twisted joy filled his eyes. He carefully lifted the tiny form, wrapped it in a clean cloth he had brought, and placed it beside her head like a precious gift. “Look what we made together, my love,” he whispered, kissing her cold forehead again. “Even now, you’re giving me everything.” He held her close, the three of them together in the dim lantern light, the air thick with the sweet-rot scent of their eternal bond.

In Wei Jie’s mind, this was true romance. Mei Ling would never leave him. She was his forever—beautiful, silent, and completely his. And she had given birth to his child.
